name: Spiral fitter, global winding fit

source.note: The volume_cartographer source-lock commit the villa image already pins, so this backend adds no second source identity to keep true.

required_inputs_note: Paths under the run's dataset_path, checked before a GPU is claimed. A dataset missing any of them is refused by name rather than discovered by upstream several minutes into the fit.

upstream_module_constants.note: These six select the scroll and are assigned at module level in fit_spiral.py, evaluated at import. None is a default_config key, so FIT_SPIRAL_CONFIG_OVERRIDES cannot reach them -- upstream's own validator raises KeyError on anything outside that dict.

scroll_binding.how: The six are located as module-level assignments by their position in the parse tree and replaced with literals, into a copy. The image keeps the bytes its source lock verified; the run reads the rewritten file, and the receipt carries both digests so which script ran is answerable from the record alone.
scroll_binding.all_or_nothing: A run names all six. Half a binding fits a new dataset over Scroll 1's z range at Scroll 1's voxel size, which produces surfaces, costs a GPU-day and means nothing.
scroll_binding.defaults_note: Only the winding sense carries a default, because CW is upstream's and a fit run with the wrong one is visibly wrong rather than quietly so. The other five are deliberately empty: defaulting them to Scroll 1's would make a forgotten field fit the wrong scroll under the right name.
refuses: a constant that is absent, shadowed or computed rather than written out -- upstream moving past the pinned commit must stop the run, not leave it at Scroll 1
a rewrite that does not read back as the values asked for
z_end at or below z_begin, a voxel size that is not positive, an empty scroll name, a winding sense outside CW and CCW

outputs.note: The per-winding TIFXYZ is what makes this a P1 backend at all: it is the same artifact seed-grow produces, so it enters the same P2 certification gate rather than a parallel one.

notes.config_overrides: disable_patches only, which is the basic workflow the tutorial describes -- fit on point collections and tracks, load no verified or unverified patches. Every other one of the 105 keys is left at upstream's default, frozen for comparability rather than tuned.
notes.gpu: Required. This is a fitting run, not a local grow.
notes.status: SELECTABLE_NOT_DEFAULT: upstream recommends this method, the scroll is now selectable, and it runs from the P1 queue in helena-villa-python. Not the default because no frozen reference control has compared it against vc3d-m7-seed-grow on this corpus.

non_claims: a fitted spiral is not physical-QC acceptance, not ink, and not text; it is geometry and enters the same certification gate as any other surface
no comparison against vc3d-m7-seed-grow has been run on this corpus; this profile makes the comparison possible and records nothing about which backend is better
the required_inputs are the paths the script reads at the pinned commit, not a claim that Campaign X currently holds them for any scroll

a scroll being selectable is not a claim that the fit is good on it: upstream's own validation is on their example, and the rebind moves the code to another dataset without moving any evidence with it
superseded_note: Required all nine input paths, which the code does not: the four point-collection files degrade a fit rather than stopping one. Kept readable; nothing should be queued against it.
